target_customer: Landlords and tenants, and later buyers and sellers, in Chile, Mexico and Colombia
problem: Renting or selling a home in Latin America meant slow brokers, guarantors and paperwork; Houm digitised listing, showing, contract and rent collection.
business_model: real estate brokerage commissions and property management fees
product_category: digital real estate marketplace and brokerage (proptech)

founders.name: Benjamín Labra
education: MSc in Real Estate Development, Columbia University
founders.background_notes: YC page describes investment banking, real estate development, asset management and finance experience without naming employers; TechCrunch calls him a longtime real estate developer.

founders.name: Nicolás Knockaert
education: MSc in Real Estate, Columbia University
founders.background_notes: YC page reports 12+ years in real estate development, investments and proptech.

competitors.name: QuintoAndar
competitors.what: Brazilian digital rental and sale platform that TechCrunch called very similar to Houm
competitors.traction_then: described as dominating its home market

technical_complexity.rationale: A marketplace with scheduling, a pricing algorithm built on market data and contract flows is standard engineering; the difficulty was operations across cities (about 200 staff plus 200 freelance Houmers in 2021).

defensibility.rationale: Listing portals and brokerages are copyable; the operating network of property showers and local data gives limited protection.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Brazilian players expanded into Mexico around 2021 (Loft bought TrueHome per an onlinemarketplaces summary); Houm itself continued independently, with no acquisition found.

market_need_then: Rental and sale processes in Chile, Mexico and Colombia were paper heavy and guarantor dependent; Houm showed a property every eight minutes by May 2021 according to its CEO in TechCrunch.

branding.name_origin: Launched in 2018 as Arriendo Asegurado, a descriptive name; renamed Houm around 2020 because the founders did not want a name to limit them, found Houm friendlier and more memorable, and say it sounds like the English word home (as reported in Chilean press seen in search results).

identity.voice_and_tone: Warm, friendly and aspirational per the company site, with Spanish greetings, emojis and family-home framing.

branding.brand_signature: Homophone of home as the brand idea

rebrands.why: Descriptive name limited growth and was less friendly and memorable, per founders in press

branding.community_and_virality: In June 2022 Houm pledged to donate 1 percent of monthly revenue to people applying for a home, per Forbes Chile search result; no fan community found.

brand_strength.rationale: A deliberate rebrand to a friendlier name and consistent warm voice, plus regional press; no evidence of fan community or virality.

pivots.from: Arriendo Asegurado, rental insurance and rental management
pivots.to: Houm, digital marketplace for renting, buying and selling
pivots.why: Not stated beyond not wanting the name to limit growth

outcome_analysis: Houm raised 1.3 million dollars in 2020, an 8 million dollar seed in May 2021 after Y Combinator, and a 35 million dollar Series A in November 2021 led by Goodwater, to expand to 15 cities across Chile, Mexico and Colombia. The founders had real estate backgrounds. The company is active with a reported team of 400, but no later funding was found and 2022 proptech distress elsewhere in Latin America suggests a hard environment; the current financial health is unknown.
notes: Series A and seed each stated by TechCrunch and LatamList (search results); 1.3 million round dated from Magma post published May 2020, exact close unknown. Total raised 45 million per TechCrunch and houm.com; a later press release claims more than 50 million, unverified. YC page and houm.com differ on YC year (houm.com says 2020, YC says W21). Aptuno and La Haus appeared in an undated 2021 summary as nearby rivals but are not listed as competitors because the source was not dated.
